Read-only pyreadstat coverage scan of only the accepted COMP.FUNDA columns and filters: FY1998–FY2003 had 12,554; 12,531; 12,093; 11,584; 11,253; and 11,067 source rows, respectively, with no repeated gvkey–fyear keys in those years.

Fresh controller-native SAS build and Stata cell log: source and handoff unchanged; Stata marker reports 107,546 estimation observations in FY1979–1998 and 32,287 in FY1999–2003, last added FY2003. Fresh aggregate table is work/artifacts/s1_aggregate.csv.
changes: Extended the existing SAS source-year bound from FY1978–1998 to FY1978–2003 and the current-year pair window from FY1979–1998 to FY1979–2003; the original FY1979 start and FY1978 lag input remain.

Rebuilt the historical and added fiscal years jointly from the named current local COMP.FUNDA file. Preserved the accepted population filters, annual lag construction, same-currency rule, screens, pooled 0.5th/99.5th percentile trimming, and pooled OLS specification. The trim cutoffs are recomputed on the extended pooled sample.
Retained numeric fyear in the SAS handoff and counted actual Stata e(sample) rows by fiscal year. Added an aggregate-only CSV fit export under work/artifacts.
limitations: The local COMP.FUNDA is a current-vintage source, not verified as the paper’s 1999 PST/full-coverage population. The current xsga and sale labels match the paper’s SG&A and sales roles, but their historical item-number crosswalks to #189 and #12 remain unverified.
The exact industrial-firm inclusion rule is not reported; accepted construction uses indfmt=INDL as its documented approximation. Percentile tie handling is also not specified by the paper.

For unlike-currency adjacent-year pairs, the accepted construction cannot establish the arithmetic direction of CURRTR and leaves the monetary ratios unavailable. This limitation remains in the extension.
Table 2 reports t-statistics without identifying its covariance procedure. The replay retains the accepted best-effort conventional homoskedastic OLS standard errors.

The accepted FY1979–1998 run had 109,388 source-screened rows and 107,562 trimmed unit-verified fit observations, versus the paper’s 64,663 and 63,958. In the extended pooled fit, 107,546 of 139,833 observations are from FY1979–1998 and 32,287 are added FY1999–2003; the 16-row difference in the old-period count follows recomputing the pooled trim cutoffs. Current-vintage population differences limit numerical comparability.

The saved predecessor and extended beta estimates use the same estimator and variable definitions, but their estimation samples differ because the latter adds five fiscal years and recalculates pooled trimming cutoffs; the coefficient change is not an isolated estimate on a fixed set of historical rows.
